# ffmpeg-render-pro

ffmpeg-render-pro is a Node.js toolkit for parallel video rendering: it splits a frame
range across worker threads, encodes one MP4 segment per worker via ffmpeg, and joins
the segments with stream copy (no re-encode). It includes cross-platform GPU encoder
detection (NVENC, VideoToolbox, AMF, VA-API, QSV), a live localhost dashboard, a
checkpoint system for long renders, color grading and audio merge helpers, a CLI, and
an MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio server. Requires Node.js >= 18 and ffmpeg
(on PATH, or pointed to via FFMPEG_RENDER_PRO_FFMPEG). Version 1.5.0. MIT license.

## Install

- npm (global CLI + MCP binary): `npm install -g ffmpeg-render-pro`
- npm (library): `npm install ffmpeg-render-pro`
- Claude Code MCP: `claude mcp add --transport stdio ffmpeg-render-pro -- ffmpeg-render-pro-mcp`
- Claude Code MCP without global install: `claude mcp add --transport stdio ffmpeg-render-pro -- npx --yes --package=ffmpeg-render-pro ffmpeg-render-pro-mcp`

## MCP tools (7)

- detect_gpu: probe the best hardware video encoder on this machine (each call re-probes and refreshes a 7-day cache that system_info reads)
- system_info: CPU cores, RAM, recommended worker count for a resolution, ffmpeg version
- render_video: parallel render from a worker script; progress notifications + cancellation
- get_worker_template: the worker contract plus bundled reference worker source (templatePath is directly usable as worker_script)
- color_grade: apply a preset (noir, warm, cool, cinematic, vintage) or custom -vf filter
- merge_audio: mux an audio file into a video (video stream-copied, audio AAC)
- concat_videos: stream-copy join videos; ffprobe compatibility validation on by default

All tools return structuredContent matching a declared outputSchema, so parse JSON
instead of scraping text. Writers overwrite output_path. render_video defaults to
30 fps (the CLI render command defaults to 60). stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames.

## CLI quickstart

- `ffmpeg-render-pro info` (system snapshot)
- `ffmpeg-render-pro detect-gpu` (probe hardware encoders; --cpu / --gpu force modes)
- `ffmpeg-render-pro benchmark --duration=5` (test render with the bundled worker)
- `ffmpeg-render-pro render worker.js --duration=60 --output=out.mp4 --crf=18 --encoder-preset=slow`
- Headless: add `--no-dashboard --linger-ms=0`

## Worker contract (render_video / renderParallel)

A worker script runs as a Node worker_thread. workerData fields injected:
width, height, fps, seed, startFrame, endFrame (exclusive), segmentPath, workerId,
totalFrames, duration, plus any extra keys passed via renderParallel({ workerData }).
The worker must render frames [startFrame, endFrame), encode them to an MP4 at
segmentPath (the reference worker pipes raw BGRA to ffmpeg), and post messages:

- { type: 'progress', workerId, pct, fps, frame, eta } periodically
- { type: 'done', workerId } exactly once when the segment is fully written
- { type: 'error', workerId, error } on failure (never done after error)
- { type: 'fast-forward-start', workerId, frames } optional, before state replay

All segments must share codec, resolution, framerate, and pixel format (they are
stream-copy concatenated). Deterministic output requires deriving all randomness
from the injected seed.

## Library entry points

require('ffmpeg-render-pro') exports: renderParallel, createEncoder, detectGPU,
getConfig, computeTotalFrames, concatSegments, colorGrade, mergeAudio,
startDashboard, ProgressTracker, saveCheckpoint, loadCheckpoint, restoreCheckpoint,
generateCheckpoints, getEncoderIO, getCodecArgs, ffmpegBin, ffprobeBin, and more.
renderParallel options include signal (AbortSignal) and quiet (byte-clean stdout).
